comment: SL-03: OpenZeppelin 5.0.2 Math.mulDiv intentionally uses XOR to seed the inverse modulo 2^256, then refines it using Newton-Raphson; exponentiation would break the algorithm. Pinned dependency source comments explain the seed. AC28 and AC45 exercise rounding/solvency.
reviewed_description:
Math.mulDiv(uint256,uint256,uint256) (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol#123-202) has bitwise-xor operator ^ instead of the exponentiation operator **: 
	 - inverse = (3 * denominator) ^ 2 (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol#184)

comment: SL-05: OpenZeppelin Math.mulDiv first subtracts the remainder, so division by the factored power of two is exact. The subsequent multiplication seeds/refines the inverse modulo 2^256, not ordinary arithmetic on a truncated quotient. Pinned 5.0.2 source comments explain the algorithm; AC28 and AC45 exercise rounding/solvency.
reviewed_description:
Math.mulDiv(uint256,uint256,uint256) (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol#123-202) performs a multiplication on the result of a division:
	- denominator = denominator / twos (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol#169)
	- inverse *= 2 - denominator * inverse (node_modules/@openzeppelin/contracts/utils/math/Math.sol#192)

comment: SL-20: The reported pre-accounting call is token.burn during auto-finalization. token is immutable and constructed as LaunchToken; pinned OpenZeppelin ERC20 burn only updates balances and emits Transfer, with no callback. withdrawProceeds is nonReentrant and sets proceedsWithdrawn before the ETH call. AC42 and owner/mixed-role AC47 tests cover payout protection.

comment: SL-21: The reported pre-claimed call is the immutable LaunchToken burn during auto-finalization, which has no callback. claim is nonReentrant and marks all bids claimed before token transfer or ETH refund. AC37, AC38 and claim/mixed-role AC47 tests cover it.

	- require(bool,string)(token.transfer(msg.sender,totalTokens),token transfer) (contracts/DutchAuction.sol#255)

comment: SL-39: The warning concerns versions allowed by ^0.8.20. Actual compilation is 0.8.24: VerbatimInvalidDeduplication was fixed in 0.8.23; FullInlinerNonExpressionSplitArgumentEvaluationOrder and MissingSideEffectsOnSelectorAccess in 0.8.21. Solidity's bug list confirms these fixes; not a claim that all compiler bugs are absent.

comment: SL-43: Low-level ETH call supports contract recipients without a fixed gas stipend. Success is checked and a failure reverts accounting atomically; all production payment entry points use nonReentrant. A rejecting recipient can prevent its own payout/refund (an owner contract can also block its owner payout). AC29, AC38, AC42-44 and AC47 cover normal payouts and reentry; rejecting-recipient behavior is accepted, not claimed covered.
